0.0.n: Used with ございます to make a polite morning greeting.

0.1.n: ござい is part of ございます, which makes おはよう polite; it is not a separate word here.

0.2.n: Completes ございます in the polite morning greeting.

0.4.n: A standard daytime greeting; the final は is pronounced わ.

0.6.m: start of the name えむえむ
0.6.n: This segment is only the beginning of the speaker’s name, not a hesitation sound.

0.7.n: むえむ completes the name えむえむ, and です makes the self-introduction polite.

1.0.n: Introduces what the speaker will cover in this video.

1.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic of the sentence.

1.2.n: The prefix お gives 仕事 a softer, more polite tone.

1.3.n: Marks お仕事 as what exists or is scheduled.

1.4.n: Literally expresses existence; お仕事がある describes having work scheduled.

1.5.n: The preceding お仕事がある describes which days the speaker means.

1.6.n: Links workdays to the morning routine followed on those days.

1.7.n: An expression borrowed from English and written in katakana.

1.8.n: Marks the morning routine as what the speaker will introduce.

1.9.n: 紹介する becomes polite 紹介します to announce what the speaker will present.

2.0.n: Combines with する to form a verb about sleeping past the intended time.

2.1.n: The negative linking form of する makes 寝坊しないで mean without oversleeping.

2.3.n: Emphasizes successfully getting up as intended, rather than sleeping late.

2.4.n: Casual past ability form of 起きる; standard 起きられた loses ら in everyday speech.

2.5.n: 起きれた describes days when the speaker successfully got up.

2.6.n: Connects the described days to their morning routine.

2.7.n: This borrowed expression names the routine being shown.

2.8.n: Politely finishes the statement identifying this as a particular morning routine.

3.0.n: A product name referring to the phone the speaker uses for alarms.

3.1.n: Connects iPhone with its alarm function.

3.2.n: Short for 目覚まし時計, but here it refers to the phone’s alarm.

3.3.n: Marks the alarm as the means of waking up.

3.4.n: The speaker explicitly refers to herself here.

3.5.n: Marks 私 as the topic before explaining her waking habit.

3.6.n: 起きる in the ている form describes a repeated habit here, not being awake right now.

3.7.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before です.

3.8.n: Makes the explanation with ん polite.

3.9.n: Links this explanation to the upcoming difficulty with waking up.

4.0.n: 回 counts occurrences, here one sounding of the alarm.

4.1.n: Casual contraction of では; sets one alarm occurrence as an insufficient condition.

4.2.n: Strengthens the negative claim that follows.

4.3.n: Casual negative ability form of 起きる; standard 起きられない loses ら.

4.4.n: Introduces the reason for setting multiple alarms in the next line.

5.0.n: Shares the counter 回 with the following number to give an approximate range.

5.2.n: Together, ２、３回 means roughly two or three occurrences.

5.4.n: Signals that the speaker is correcting her previous estimate.

5.5.n: Pairs with ５回 to give the revised approximate number.

5.7.n: The counter 回 applies to both four and five in this range.

5.8.n: Emphasizes four or five as a minimum rather than an exact count.

5.9.n: An English loanword; Japanese does not require a plural ending here.

5.10.n: Marks アラーム as what the speaker sets.

5.11.n: Combines with する to form the verb セットする.

5.12.n: The て-form of する links setting alarms with waking up.

5.13.n: Polite ている form of 起きる describes her usual waking routine.

0.lit: Good morning, hello. I am えむえむ.
0.tip: えむえむ is the speaker’s name, even though the word segments split it awkwardly.

1.lit: This time, I will introduce the morning routine for days when I have work.
1.tip: お仕事がある comes before 日 to describe which days: days when there is work.

2.lit: It is the morning routine for days I managed to get up properly without oversleeping.
2.tip: しないで means without doing, so 寝坊しないで means without oversleeping.

3.lit: With my iPhone’s alarm, I wake up, you see, but…
3.tip: ている describes a regular habit here, rather than an action happening at this moment.

4.lit: Because with one time, I definitely cannot wake up…
4.tip: 起きれない is the common casual version of 起きられない, meaning cannot wake up.

5.lit: Two, three times—no, at least four, five times—I set alarms and wake up.
5.tip: は after a quantity can emphasize a minimum: here, at least four or five times.
